newsitem.title: USA: Boston mayor rebuts anti-convention study - paper.
newsitem.headline: Boston mayor rebuts anti-convention study - paper.

text.p: Boston's Mayor, who supports plans for a new and bigger convention center, cast doubts on a study to be released later this week that questions whether it should be financed, Boston Globe reported Tuesday.

Aides to Mayor Thomas Menino said the city's lack of convention space was causing would-be exhibitors to reject Boston as a location, not its lack of a warm climate and a theme park, key attractions of other sites.
The new study said an increasing number of cities are building bigger convention sites, making it harder to win the business, according to the paper.
A preliminary state-city study last month predicted the new convention center would create $436 million a year in new business and 6,800 new jobs.

The mayor placed plans to build the $650 million convention center in South Boston at the top of his agenda and has won support from Gov. William Weld, Senate President Thomas Birmingham and House Speaker Thomas Finneran, according to the Globe.
